heroSub: Six low-budget stays in Kamphaeng Phet we've reviewed, every one scoring 7.8 or higher — from a fresh budget chain that's the highest-rated stay in town and private garden bungalows to a warm owner-run guesthouse from ฿550, plus a newly opened riverside hotel, a central walking-street stay, and European-themed bungalows with a pool. introH2: 🏯 Can you do Kamphaeng Phet on a small budget — and how do you pick for value?
introHtml: Kamphaeng Phet is a World Heritage town that many people stay in for a single night on the way north, so rooms cost far less than the big tourist cities — a few hundred to just over a thousand baht still gets you a well-rated room, from warm owner-run garden guesthouses and private garden bungalows to a fresh budget chain, plus a riverside hotel and themed bungalows with a pool. The trick to booking for value is to weigh three things — the real review score against the price (a stay from ฿700 that scores 9.4 beats a pricier one), matching the area to your plans (in town you can walk or cycle to the Historical Park and the walking street, while the edge-of-town stays need a car), and what you're willing to trade off (budget guesthouses and bungalows often have no pool or breakfast). This guide rounds up 6 budget stays in Kamphaeng Phet, every one scoring 7.8 or higher and bookable on all 3 sites — ranked by value, with the honest pros and cons, prices compared on 3 sites, and direct booking links.
mrtHtml: Kamphaeng Phet has no metro and no commercial airport — the main way in is driving yourself or taking a coach into the town centre, and almost every stay has free parking, so they suit self-drivers well. Pick by your trip: in town near the Historical Park lets you walk and cycle to the World Heritage ruins and the walking street (Three J, Navarat) · the Asia Highway side is easy in and out of town, handy for a stopover and self-drivers (Hop Inn, Bunraksa) · Nakhon Chum on the Ping River is quiet, with river views (J2) · riverside near the Historical Park has a resort feel with a pool (Scenic) · without a car, base yourself in town at Three J or Navarat, within reach of food and near the Historical Park; the suburban and Asia Highway stays are far easier with a car.

entries.addr: 88 Ratchawithi Rd Soi 1, Nai Mueang, Mueang Kamphaeng Phet
entries.storyHtml: Hop Inn is the highest-scoring stay of any Kamphaeng Phet hotel we've reviewed — 9.4 from 47 reviews, from just ฿700. It's a newly opened branch of the budget chain, so the rooms are fresh and spotless, the beds comfy and the hot water strong, and you know exactly what you get. It sits on the Asia Highway side, easy in and out of town and near the malls, with free parking — we rank it the best value in this guide because it earns the top score at a budget price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The walls only muffle sound so-so, so if you're a light sleeper ask for a higher floor or a room off the main corridor and pack earplugs · There's no breakfast, but you can walk to the Chakungrao night bazaar or the eateries around the malls · Book ahead and compare all 3 sites first.

entries.name: Bunraksa Resort
entries.revCount: 9.1 · 86 reviews · private bungalows with a kitchenette
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Nakhon Chum · Asia Highway side · suburban Kamphaeng Phet
tags: 🍳 Kitchenette and fridge in the room
entries.storyHtml: Bunraksa is a garden-bungalow resort that scores a high 9.1 from 86 reviews, from just ฿650. Its standout is private, standalone brick bungalows with a small kitchenette and fridge in the room, a garden porch to sit out on, and parking right at your door. It sits in the Nakhon Chum area on the Asia Highway side, easy in and out of town — a value pick for self-drivers who want a private little house at a budget price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: There's a kitchenette and fridge in the room, so for a longer stay you can buy groceries and cook, since there's no breakfast · The bungalows sit in a garden by nature, so close the doors tight and bring insect repellent · There are only a few units, so book ahead on long weekends.
pros: High score, 9.1 from 86 reviews · low starting price ฿650
Private standalone bungalows with a kitchenette and fridge
Quiet garden setting, park at your door, owner-run
Near the Asia Highway, easy in and out of town
cons: Suburban Nakhon Chum, so you drive into the old town and the Historical Park
In a garden by nature, so there are some mosquitoes (from reviews)

entries.addr: 79 Ratchawithi Rd Soi 1, Nai Mueang, Mueang Kamphaeng Phet
entries.storyHtml: Three J is the cheapest stay in this guide (฿550) and the most reviewed, at 200 reviews, scoring 8.7. It's a family-run garden guesthouse where the owner and his son speak good English and look after guests like family; the rooms are small but clean, and there are bikes to rent. Its in-town spot on Ratchawithi Road Soi 1 is a ~3 km cycle from the World Heritage Historical Park — a fit for backpackers and anyone wanting to soak up the old town slowly.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you like privacy, take a standalone garden Bungalow — it's quieter and shaded by trees · Rent a bike to ride the Historical Park; it's how many people love to see Kamphaeng Phet · There are only about 12 rooms, so book ahead in high season.
pros: Cheapest in the set, ฿550 · most reviewed, 200, scoring 8.7
Family-run garden guesthouse, warm English-speaking owners (from reviews)
In-town location, cycle to the Historical Park
Standalone bungalows, bikes to rent, free parking

Only about 12 rooms, fills fast in high season

entries.storyHtml: J2 Hotel is a 2024 riverside opening that pairs fresh, clean rooms with a mid-range price just right — 8.7 from 96 reviews, from ฿850. It's a smart white building with new rooms and full fittings; some Grand Deluxe rooms have a Ping River balcony, and there's a Family Suite with bunk beds for families. It sits on the Nakhon Chum side with a big, secure car park — a value pick if you want to step up from budget to a new riverside room.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For a view, ask for a Grand Deluxe on the river side when you book, since not every room sees the water · For a family, the Family Suite with bunk beds beats booking two rooms · Breakfast is à la carte, so the choice is limited.

cons: On the Nakhon Chum side, so you drive across the bridge to the Historical Park

entries.name: Navarat Heritage Hotel
entries.revCount: 8.2 · 96 reviews · by the walking street, town centre
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Town centre · on the Ping River · by the walking street
tags: 🚶 By the Kamphaeng Phet walking street
entries.addr: 2 Soi 21, Thesa 1 Rd, Nai Mueang, Mueang Kamphaeng Phet
entries.storyHtml: Navarat Heritage is a 3-star town-centre hotel right by the walking street and the Ping River, scoring 8.2 from 96 reviews, from ฿1,000. It's long-standing but renovated in 2020, so the rooms are more spacious and cleaner than you'd expect, with an in-house café, a gym and free bikes to borrow. Its strength is being able to walk to the walking street, food and the riverfront without driving, with the Historical Park a ~3 km cycle away — a fit for anyone without a car who wants to stay central.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: It's an old building renovated, so ask for a refurbished room away from the walking street for a fresher, quieter stay · Borrow a free bike to ride along the river or to the Historical Park in the cool early morning · Breakfast costs extra.
pros: Central location, by the walking street and the Ping River
Spacious rooms, renovated in 2020, scoring 8.2
Café, gym, free bikes to borrow, free parking
Walk and cycle to sights without driving
cons: An old building renovated; some rooms feel dated or musty (from reviews)

entries.storyHtml: Scenic Riverside is a boutique bungalow resort with a European-town theme on the Ping River, scoring 7.8 from 23 reviews, from ฿1,200. Each bungalow is styled after a different city (Amsterdam, Zurich, Matterhorn) with its own rooftop for a BBQ over the river, and there's an outdoor pool — rare at this price. It's in the town area near the Historical Park; we place it last because it's the priciest in the set and reviews flag inconsistent upkeep.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: It's a long-running resort with uneven upkeep, so check the latest photos and reviews before booking and choose a free-cancellation rate in case the condition isn't as expected · For the riverside feel and a BBQ, take the Riverside Bungalow · Ask the resort which unit is in good shape and which theme is free before you book.

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are approximate starting rates outside peak season and can change by date and season — always check live prices and compare 3 sites before booking. The scores and highlights here come from reading real guest reviews on the booking platforms, not from staying ourselves. Every stay here scores 7.8+ but is budget 2–3 star, so each has trade-offs for the price — small guesthouse rooms, no pool or breakfast at some, or a suburban spot that isn't walkable to the sights; read each one's honest caveats before booking. All 6 can be compared across all 3 sites (Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com). Rooms fill fast on long weekends and holidays, especially the in-town and Ping Riverfront stays, so book ahead. faqTitle: FAQ — common traveller questions about budget hotels in Kamphaeng Phet

faq.q: ❓ Which budget hotel in Kamphaeng Phet is the best value?
faq.a: Going by value (score for the price), Hop Inn from ฿700 scoring 9.4 is the best value in this set — it's the highest-rated of any Kamphaeng Phet stay we've reviewed, at a budget price. For the lowest price, Three J Guesthouse from ฿550 (8.7, most reviewed at 200) and Bunraksa Resort ฿650, private bungalows (9.1), are also great value.

faq.q: ❓ How much do budget hotels in Kamphaeng Phet cost?
faq.a: In this guide, prices start around ฿550–1,200/night. The cheapest are Three J from ฿550, Bunraksa ฿650 and Hop Inn ฿700; the riverside and town-centre picks are J2 ฿850, Navarat ฿1,000 and Scenic ฿1,200. All are approximate off-peak starting rates — rates rise and rooms fill fast on long weekends and holidays.

faq.q: ❓ Which area should I stay in in Kamphaeng Phet on a budget?
faq.a: It depends on your plans — in town near the Historical Park lets you walk and cycle to the World Heritage ruins and the walking street (Three J, Navarat) · the Asia Highway side is easy in and out of town, handy for a stopover and self-drivers (Hop Inn, Bunraksa) · Nakhon Chum on the Ping River is quiet with water views (J2) · riverside near the Historical Park has a resort feel with a pool (Scenic).

faq.q: ❓ Where should I stay in Kamphaeng Phet without a car?
faq.a: Without a car, stay in town at Navarat Heritage, by the walking street and the Ping River within reach of food, or Three J Guesthouse in town with bikes to rent for the Historical Park. Both let you walk and cycle to the sights without driving. The suburban and Asia Highway stays (Hop Inn, Bunraksa) are much easier with a car.

faq.q: ❓ Are there budget stays in Kamphaeng Phet with a pool?
faq.a: Yes · Scenic Riverside Resort ฿1,200 is a European-themed bungalow resort on the Ping River with an outdoor pool, rare at this price (though check the latest photos and reviews first, as upkeep is uneven). The cheaper stays (budget hotels, guesthouses, bungalows) mostly have no pool and lean on location and value instead.

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest to book a Kamphaeng Phet hotel?
faq.a: Prices differ across each site (Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com) by promotion at the time, so open and compare all 3 before booking — all 6 stays in this guide can be compared across all 3 sites, and each review page has the comparison links, which can save you tens to hundreds of baht a night.
